questions.question: A maximization LP with all variables nonnegative has a canonical simplex tableau with objective row $z+\sum_{j}q_jx_j=z_0$ (sum over the nonbasic variables $x_j$). Under which condition does the simplex optimality test declare the current basic solution optimal?
options: All nonbasic $q_j$ are negative or zero, with feasible values
The tableau is feasible and no nonbasic $q_j$ is negative
Every right-hand side is nonnegative, whatever the $q_j$
Feasibility, and each nonbasic $q_j$ strictly above $0$

questions.question: A feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP (all variables nonnegative) has objective row $z+\sum_{j}q_jx_j=z_0$ (sum over the nonbasic variables $x_j$) with every $q_j\ge0$. Why does this prove that no feasible solution has a larger objective value than $z_0$?
options: Each neighbouring corner has been checked and none has more than $z_0$
Raising any single $x_j$ alone cannot help, which settles all cases
All basic variables are positive, so no resource is left to use
Every feasible point has $z=z_0-\sum_jq_jx_j$, each $q_jx_j\ge0$

questions.question: For a maximization LP, a tableau's objective row still contains a basic variable with a nonzero coefficient, while all nonbasic coefficients are $\ge0$. Why can the optimality test not be applied to it yet?
options: The test needs every coefficient in the row to be strictly positive
The right-hand side $z_0$ must be zero before the test can be used
$z$ still depends on a basic variable, so the signs give no bound
Basic variables in the row make the basic solution infeasible

questions.question: A canonical tableau of a maximization LP has every nonbasic objective-row coefficient $q_j\ge0$, but one constraint row has right-hand side $-2$. Why does the optimality test not apply?
options: The basic solution has a value $-2<0$, so it is not feasible
A negative right-hand side makes some $q_j$ negative as well
The test requires every right-hand side to be at least $1$
It does apply: the value $z_0$ is then the optimal value of the LP

questions.question: A feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP has every nonbasic $q_j\ge0$, and one basic variable has value $0$. Does the optimality test still certify the current solution as optimal?
options: No: every basic value must be strictly positive for the test
Yes: a basic value of zero is still feasible, so the test applies
No: a zero basic value turns the test into a necessary condition
Yes, but only if that basic variable is a slack variable

questions.question: A feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP has objective row $z+2x_1+0s_2+3s_1=12$, with nonbasic variables $x_1,s_1,s_2$. What does the optimality test conclude?
options: Not optimal, since $s_2$ has coefficient $0$, not positive
Not optimal, since $x_1$ is nonbasic at $0$
Optimal, but only if every $q_j$ were positive
Optimal, since every nonbasic coefficient is $\ge0$

questions.question: After an iteration of simplex on a maximization LP, the feasible canonical tableau shows $z-x_2+4s_1=20$ as objective row; $x_2$ and $s_1$ are nonbasic. Is optimality certified?
options: Optimal: the coefficient $4$ outweighs the $-1$
No certificate, since $x_2$ has a negative $q$
Optimal: one negative coefficient is allowed
Not optimal: $s_1$ has a positive coefficient

questions.question: A feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP with nonnegative variables has objective row $z+2s_1+5s_2=40$, with $s_1,s_2$ nonbasic. What upper bound on $z$ over all feasible solutions does it certify?
options: $z\le2$

questions.question: For a maximization LP with slacks $s_1,s_2$, the final tableau has objective row $z+2s_1+5s_2=40$. A feasible plan leaves $s_1=3$ and $s_2=1$ units of the two resources unused. What is its objective value?

For a maximization LP, the current feasible canonical tableau expresses the objective as $z=50-3s_1+2x_2$, with $s_1,x_2$ nonbasic. Written as $z+\sum_jq_jx_j=z_0$, what does the optimality test conclude?
options: Optimal: $q_{x_2}=2\ge0$ as read from $z=50-3s_1+2x_2$
Not optimal: $q_{s_1}=-3$ is negative in the row
Optimal: $z_0=50$ is positive, so no gain is left
Not optimal: $q_{x_2}=-2$ in the row $z+3s_1-2x_2=50$

questions.question: An optimal feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP has every nonbasic $q_j\ge0$, and the nonbasic variable $x_3$ has $q_3=0$. What does $q_3=0$ indicate?
options: The tableau is not yet optimal until $x_3$ gets a positive $q_3$
The current optimum is unique, since no $q_j$ is negative
Possibly another optimum, if $x_3$ can rise by a positive amount
Raising $x_3$ will increase $z$, so it should enter

questions.question: A feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP (all variables nonnegative) has objective row $z+\sum_{j}q_jx_j=z_0$ (sum over the nonbasic variables $x_j$) with every nonbasic $q_j>0$ strictly. What follows about the current basic feasible solution?
options: It is optimal, and every other feasible point has $z<z_0$
It is optimal, but other feasible points with $z=z_0$ may exist
It is optimal only among the corners of the region
Strict positivity is needed before the test applies

questions.question: The certificate $z=z_0-\sum_jq_jx_j\le z_0$ for a maximization tableau with all nonbasic $q_j\ge0$ uses that every variable is nonnegative. What breaks if a nonbasic variable with $q_j>0$ were allowed to be negative?
options: Nothing, since only the signs of the $q_j$ matter
Lowering it below $0$ would raise $z$ above $z_0$
The tableau would no longer be canonical
Raising it above $0$ would then raise $z$

questions.question: To minimize a cost, the simplex method maximizes $z=-\text{cost}$. A feasible canonical tableau has objective row $z+s_1+2s_2=-18$, with $s_1,s_2$ nonbasic. What does the optimality test give for the minimum cost?
options: Optimal; the minimum cost equals $18$
Optimal; the cost is $z_0=-18$
Not yet optimal, as $z_0=-18$ is negative
Optimal, at a cost of $18+1+2=21$

questions.question: For $\max\ 5x_1+4x_2$ with $6x_1+4x_2+s_1=24$ and $x_1+2x_2+s_2=6$, the final tableau has objective row $z+\frac{3}{4}s_1+\frac{1}{2}s_2=21$. A manager proposes $(x_1,x_2)=(2,3)$ with value $22$. What explains the conflict?
options: The certificate is wrong, so the optimum is at least $22$
$(2,3)$ is feasible and ties, since both give $z\le22$
The value of $(2,3)$ is really $21$, not $22$
$(2,3)$ gives $s_2=-2<0$, so it is infeasible

questions.question: For $\max\ 5x_1+4x_2$ with $6x_1+4x_2+s_1=24$ and $x_1+2x_2+s_2=6$ (slacks $s_1,s_2\ge0$), the final tableau has objective row $z+\frac{3}{4}s_1+\frac{1}{2}s_2=21$. What is the largest value $z$ can have among feasible plans that leave at least $4$ units of resource $1$ unused ($s_1\ge4$)?

In a feasible canonical maximization tableau, the nonbasic $x_2$ has $q_2<0$, but raising $x_2$ by any positive amount would immediately make a basic variable, currently equal to $0$, negative. What does this say about optimality?
options: The solution is certainly not optimal, since some $q_j<0$
The solution is certainly optimal, since $x_2$ cannot move
The test is silent; the current solution may still be optimal
The LP has no feasible solution, since a basic value would turn negative

questions.question: A minimization LP (all variables nonnegative) is written with $z=$ cost and a feasible canonical tableau with objective row $z+\sum_{j}q_jx_j=z_0$ (sum over the nonbasic variables $x_j$), without converting to maximization. Which sign condition on the nonbasic $q_j$ certifies optimality?
options: Every nonbasic $q_j\le0$
Every nonbasic $q_j\ge0$
Every nonbasic $q_j<0$
Every nonbasic $q_j=0$

questions.question: For $\max\ 3x_1+2x_2$ with $x_1+x_2+s_1=4$, $x_1+s_2=3$, a tableau has basic $x_2,s_2$ (current point $(0,4)$) and objective row $z+x_2+3s_1=12$, obtained by adding the first constraint to a correct row. All nonbasic coefficients are $\ge0$. What is the right conclusion?
options: Optimal with value $12$, because every nonbasic $q_j$ is $\ge0$
Not certified: the row contains basic $x_2$; $(3,1)$ gives $11$
Optimal at $(0,4)$: its value $8$ cannot be beaten
Infeasible, since the row's value $12$ exceeds the true $8$

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_1+3x_2$ with $x_1+x_2+s_1=5$ and $x_2+s_2=3$, a canonical tableau with basic $x_2,s_2$ has rows $z+x_1+3s_1=15$, $x_1+x_2+s_1=5$ and $-x_1-s_1+s_2=-2$. What is the optimal value of the LP?
options: $15$, at $(0,5)$, by the optimality test
$10$, at $(5,0)$; the corner with largest $x_1$
$13$, at $(2,3)$; the tableau certifies nothing
